---
title: "GIA model comparison"
---

This site is the documentation for
[`g-adopt/giamip`](https://github.com/g-adopt/giamip), a repository that
specifies glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA) model comparison cases and holds
the data to compare against.

The repository contains no solver. It states what to run, provides the inputs,
holds the published reference answers, and checks that a solver's output obeys
the conventions. A solver reads a case file, produces output, and is scored
here.

## Three collections

| Collection | What it is | Reference answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Spada et al. (2011)](docs/collections/spada2011.qmd) | Ten tests of GIA codes: Love numbers, relaxation spectra, the polar motion transfer function, and surface deformation for analytic loads | Published, several codes per test |
| [Martinec et al. (2018)](docs/collections/martinec2018.qmd) | Five cases (A to E) of the sea level equation, from no ocean to a moving coastline | Published. The VEGA solution is the reference |
| [GIAMIP](docs/collections/giamip.qmd) | Twelve experiments with global ice histories and present-day topography | None. This is an open intercomparison |

## Where to start

If you want to run a case, read
[what a solver must provide](docs/reference/solver-requirements.qmd) first,
then the page for the case itself.

If you want to know what a number in a data file means, read
[the column layouts](docs/reference/column-layouts.qmd) and
[the conventions](docs/reference/conventions.qmd).

If you want the data, read [fetching](docs/data/fetching.qmd). Every file is
listed with its origin and its SHA-256 sum in [the manifest](docs/data/manifest.qmd),
and every known defect in an original file is listed in
[the corrections](docs/data/corrections.qmd).
